title: They waited… but not like you think.
paragraphs: They waited… but not like you think.

No spotlight.
No stage.
No sudden explosion of power.

Just a room…
closed doors…
and hearts being undone.

We love to preach Pentecost when the fire falls in Acts 2—
the wind, the tongues, the miracle, the thousands saved.
But we skip the part that actually made it possible.
The waiting.

Acts 1:4–5 —
“Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift my Father promised…”
Wait?

After the resurrection?
After seeing Jesus alive?

Yes.
Wait.

Because heaven doesn’t release power
into unprepared vessels.
Here’s the part most people miss:

They weren’t just waiting for something.
They were being emptied of everything.

Acts 1:14 says:
“They all joined together constantly in prayer…”
Constantly.

Not casually.
Not occasionally.
This was deep surrender.
This was hidden warfare.
This was the crushing of pride, fear, ego, ambition.

Because you cannot be filled with the Holy Spirit
if you are already full of yourself.
Let’s be honest.

We want Acts 2 results
with Acts 1 discipline.

We want fire
without the altar.

We want power
without prayer.

We want influence
without intimacy.
But God doesn’t skip process.
Look closer.

Peter—the same man who denied Jesus three times
(see Luke 22:54–62)—
is now in that room.
Quiet.

No bold preaching yet.
No viral moment.

Just a broken man…
being rebuilt by grace.
This is where revival really starts.

Not on a platform.
Not in a crowd.

But in private surrender
where no one claps
and no one sees.

Psalm 51:17 —
“The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.”
That upper room?

It wasn’t just a location.
It was a condition.
A heart posture.
And then—
Suddenly.

Acts 2:2–4 —
“Suddenly a sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven… All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit…”
Suddenly.
But don’t be fooled.

What looks sudden to the crowd
was prepared in secret.

Ten days of prayer.
Ten days of surrender.
Ten days of dying to self.
And when the Spirit came?
Everything changed.

Fear turned into boldness.
Silence turned into proclamation.
Weakness turned into power.

Acts 2:41 —
“Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day.”
Three thousand.
In one day.

But it started with a room full of people
who chose to wait.
So what about you?

You’re frustrated.
Tired of waiting.
Wondering why nothing is happening.
But what if…
This is your upper room?

What if God is not delaying you—
He is preparing you?

Isaiah 40:31 —
“But those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength…”
Not waste their time.
Renew their strength.

Maybe God is dealing with hidden pride.
Maybe He’s healing wounds you buried.
Maybe He’s teaching you to depend on Him
instead of your own strength.
Because when the Spirit fills you—

It won’t just upgrade your life.
It will take over your life.
And that’s the real question:

Do you want power…
or do you want God?

Because you can chase the experience
and miss the Person.
But when you surrender to Jesus—
fully, completely, without holding back—
He doesn’t just visit you.
He transforms you.

Luke 11:13 —
“How much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!”
Ask.
But don’t just ask for power.

Ask for purity.
Ask for surrender.
Ask for a heart that can carry His presence.

Jesus died for your sin.
He rose to give you new life.
And He sent His Spirit
to live inside you—not just visit you.
This is the Gospel:

You don’t earn the fire.
You receive it through grace.

But grace will always lead you
to surrender.
So don’t run from the waiting.
Lean into it.

Turn your room into an altar.
Turn your silence into prayer.
Turn your delay into devotion.
Because when God moves—
it will be undeniable.

Pray this.
Live this.

We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
From waiting to fire—because Jesus still fills hungry hearts.
